title: The Narrowest Gate
premise: A production line needs more finished frames, but extra workers feed a review gate that can process only one frame at a time. Measuring the queue reveals the constraint and shifting effort there improves the toy flow.
hook: Why is working faster making this pile bigger?
visible_action: Wide upstream conveyors dump frames before a narrow gate; counters track arrivals, departures, and queue length.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Improving a non-constraining step may only increase waiting work.
gate: State the simulated arrival and service rates; real organizational bottlenecks require observation.

style_application.geometry: True 3D or explicitly labeled 2D isometric drawing
style_application.why: Parallel stations and the narrow gate can be inspected at the same time.
style_application.check: Distinguish projection from geometry and verify rates and queue counts.

editorial_pick.original_reason: A narrow gate is a tangible way to introduce a bottleneck and show why local speed is not enough.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Animate tokens through three stations, change only the intended capacity, and show the resulting queue.
editorial_pick.gate: Define the toy process, rates and measurement interval. Do not generalize its result to every workplace.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
